node60 · Power Distribution Node

Input Connector Survey

Part numbers, pricing, and stock for the node60's single battery input — two poles, 60 A continuous — organized by the six routes surveyed: the sealed SurLok Plus, Karl's starting idea Radlok, plain studs & ring lugs, lug-rear hybrids, TE's 2-pole MCP 9.5, and Amphenol's true 2-pole ePower-Lite, plus the China channels (Alibaba & AliExpress). No input connector is selected yet; the companion output survey is decided (genuine TE DT13-2P).

UNDECIDED — survey complete 2026-10-23; no input connector selected yet Prices & stock checked 2026-10-23 Mouser / DigiKey / Del City / LCSC

Requirement. One battery input, two poles (power + ground), 60 A continuous total (6 outputs × 10 A). The input carries fault current only until the internal LM74910H breaker (75 A setting) acts — the continuous design point is 60 A. Under-hood: −40…+125 °C ambient target (AEC-Q100 Grade 1 environment), sealed at the enclosure. The installer's battery cable is 4 AWG / 25 mm² class; the user-side part must be sourceable by the installer, or be a plain ring lug. Karl's starting idea: Amphenol Radlok. Anderson Powerpole-type connectors are excluded by Karl's preference.

Basis. All prices USD, checked 2026-10-23 at Mouser and DigiKey unless noted; LCSC checked the same day. “Per device” = both poles, mated, at the stated price break.

ROUTE 1

Amphenol SurLok Plus 5.7 mm — the sealed Radlok

Same RADSOK contact system and press-to-release latch as Radlok, in a sealed, touch-proof housing: IP67 (IP6K9K on some versions) when mated, 360° rotating plug. Manufacturer: Amphenol SurLok Plus series page ↗.

⚠️ Temperature correction (2026-10-24)

Amphenol's SurLok Plus brochure ↗ (Technical Information table) rates the 5.7 mm size −40…+105 °C in its 1,000 V DC version and −40…+125 °C only in the 1,500 V DC version — and every part costed in this route is a 1,000 V DC part. The flat −40…+125 °C figure (Amphenol's series web page) therefore does not apply to the costed parts: as costed, this route sits in the MCP 9.5 position — temperature short of the −40…+125 °C target, flagged as a potential concern, route retained for Karl's call. The 1,500 V DC variants that clear +125 °C have not been surveyed for stock or price.

5.7 mm = 120 A on 25 mm² (100 A class on 16 mm²). This is the version of Karl's Radlok idea that is specified for exposed locations. Receptacle is a flanged panel mount; rear termination choices: busbar, threaded stud (an internal ring lug bolts to it), or threaded post. Plug choices: right-angle or straight, sealed or non-sealed — the sealed plug variants are the ones to cost.

ROUTE 2

Amphenol Radlok — Karl's starting idea

RADSOK push-lock single-pole system, designed to live inside battery-pack enclosures: IP40 when mated. The feed-thru pin variant has a gasket, so the panel penetration can be sealed — but the plug-to-pin interface itself is unsealed. Family specs (datasheet Rev 1.4): −40…+125 °C, UL94 V-0, 500 mating cycles, silver-plated contacts, hex crimp. Ratings are stated on an 80 °C ambient basis and no derating curve is published — at a 125 °C ambient the margin at 60 A is unquantified, which is why the 5.7 mm size (120 A class) is the defensible pick and the 3.6 mm (70 A on 10 mm²) is not, despite 70 > 60 on paper. The receptacle is a stud feed-thru pin, not a PCB part: the internal side lands on a busbar/lug strap or the lug-end pin variant (Route 4).

The blocker is sealing, not price or availability

As an exposed under-hood input, an IP40 mated interface does not meet the requirement. Radlok only works if the input face sits inside a separately sealed region.

ROUTE 3

Studs & ring lugs — the battery cable bolts straight on

No proprietary user part at all: an insulated stud passes through the enclosure wall; the installer's battery-cable ring lug bolts on outside, a lug or busbar strap inside. This is the aftermarket/marine/truck norm. For 60 A the hardware class is 5/16″ (M8) to 3/8″ (M10) studs and 4 AWG lugs.

Engineering notes — apply to the whole route

  • Joint quality is set by torque + lock hardware (spring/Belleville washer or prevailing-torque nut) and lug plating — vibration loosening is the classic failure mode.
  • Sealing is by installation practice: gasket at the wall penetration plus a boot or adhesive heat-shrink over the external lug; there is no mated-pair IP rating.
  • The route's structural weakness for this product: almost none of this hardware publishes a temperature rating, and the one line that does (Phoenix) stops at +100 °C ambient — below the −40…+125 °C screen every connector route here meets on paper.

Spec check (run 2026-10-23)

TE's AMP MCP 9.5 tech brief rates the system at 78 A for 10 mm² wire — that clears the 60 A requirement — with a long-term operating temperature of −30…+100 °C. That range does not cover this product's −40…+125 °C under-hood target; per Karl's direction the route is retained in the survey with the temperature rating noted as a potential concern rather than scored out — adopting it would mean accepting a part whose published range stops 25 °C short of max ambient and 10 °C short of min ambient. Indicative device cost from the listed pieces is ≈$15–25 — potentially the cheapest connector route; the exact device-side/cable-side part set still needs pinning down before it can be costed exactly.

3D models — the best in this survey (official TE downloads, no account, just a terms click): 1394026-1: product/CAD page ↗ · STEP (.stp.zip) ↗ · IGES ↗. 936619-2: product/CAD page ↗ · STEP (.stp.zip) ↗ · IGES ↗. (3D PDF and 2D DXF also offered.)

Studs via China

INT

Internal termination variants — screw-clamp, stud & bolt

Surveyed 2026-10-23. Karl's framing: this whole family is one idea — a regular connector on the outside, a mechanical clamp joint on the inside instead of solder or crimp — with three flavors: bus bar rear (Route 1), threaded stud rear (Routes 1/4), and screw clamp. This section covers the screw-clamp flavor and the remaining bolted blocks at input scale.

SurLok Plus rear terminations are a closed list: threaded / crimp / busbar. Amphenol publishes no screw-clamp rear variant for the panel receptacles — if Route 1 is picked, the inside lands on a busbar, a threaded stud, or a crimp, full stop. The same holds across the industry at this scale: no 60 A-class circular/panel connector from Amphenol, TE, ITT, Harting, or Phoenix offers screw-clamp wire termination — all are crimp or solder. (The only 60 A+ panel inlets with screw terminals anywhere are IEC 60309 AC pin-and-sleeve devices — 3–5 pole AC mains hardware, +40 °C max: not this product.)

The one true match to the pattern: Harting Han Q 1/0 (Han-Modular axial-screw inserts)

A standard Han connector outside; inside, the wires land in axial screw clamps on bare conductor. 100 A / 400 V, −40…+125 °C published, IP65 with metal hoods/bases (panel-mount bases make the wall penetration).

PCB

PCB-side threaded bosses for the SurLok threaded rear (surveyed 2026-10-25)

Karl's direction (2026-10-25): the input is a SurLok Plus with the threaded rear termination — 5.7 mm, or possibly 8.0 mm — and the receptacle's threaded stud screws directly into a threaded boss soldered to the PCB, deleting the internal strap. Each boss carries the full 60 A pole current, so a published current rating is the screen that matters.

⚠️ Thread correction (datasheet check, 2026-10-25)

The thread sizes Karl started from — M4 (5.7 mm) / M6 (8.0 mm) — do not match Amphenol's SurLok Plus series datasheet (surlok_plus_series_ic_10, read in full). The datasheet prints no explicit thread callout and no pitch for the threaded rear, but its Layout Dimensions (p. 11) specify the receptacle screw-joint torque by nut size: 5.7 mm → “M6 Nut: 3 ± 0.1 N·m”; 8.0 mm → “M8 Nut: 7–8 N·m (1000 V) / 8.5 ± 0.1 N·m (1500 V)” — so the threaded studs are M6 (5.7 mm) and M8 (8.0 mm), inferred from the mating-nut callouts, not from a printed stud spec. The only M4 in the datasheet is the panel-mounting screw (both sizes) — a different feature, and the likely source of the M4 figure. Stud length is not published in the series datasheet (its dimension tables are reference-only aggregates), so thread-engagement depth against any boss remains an open measurement against the individual part drawing. Everything below is organized on the corrected M6/M8 basis.

Termination-code note (datasheet pp. 6/10). Code T (threaded) exists for both sizes at 1,000 V. At 1,500 V, the ordering table shows T only for 8.0 mm and up — the 5.7 mm 1,500 V row groups under busbar (B) only, even though screw-termination dimensions for it exist. So as published: a threaded 5.7 mm receptacle is a 1,000 V part (−40…+105 °C); a +125 °C threaded 5.7 mm needs Amphenol confirmation, while 1,500 V threaded at 8.0 mm is orderable on paper (−40…+125 °C). Temperature rows re-verified for both sizes: 1,000 V −40…+105 °C, 1,500 V −40…+125 °C.

Soldered bosses at M6 / M8 — none rated, with one exception (2026-10-26)

The soldered-boss families cap below the corrected thread sizes: Würth REDCUBE THR stops at M5, REDCUBE SMT (WP-SMBU) at M5 class, and every SMT-nut line surveyed (PEM SMTSO/SMTSOB, Würth WA-SMSI, Bossard SMT) tops out at M4. No catalog solder boss with a published current rating exists at M6 or M8 — with one exception found later: the Würth WP-SMRT reverse-SMT bush at M6 (next subsection). The other solder routes at the real thread sizes are un-rated: custom-turned bosses (China, below) or a plain brass nut/boss soldered down as a fabrication exercise. The assembly torques argue the same way for those — 3.0 N·m (M6) and 7–8.5 N·m (M8) into a solder joint whose best published torque-out (PEM, M4, FR-4) is 3.0 N·m leaves no margin at M6 and nothing at M8; the WP-SMRT is again the exception, publishing 3.9 N·m for its own joint.

The exception — Würth WP-SMRT reverse-SMT bush at M6 (added 2026-10-26, Karl's find)

PartMountThreadPublished currentKey dataPrice / stock
Würth REDCUBE SMT Reverse 74660016 / 74660016R (WP-SMRT)Würth SMT reflow (bulk / tape & reel — same part) M6, through thread, 5.6 mm long 85 A @20 °C Brass/tin, −55…+150 °C; tightening torque 3.9 N·m published; flange Ø12.0 on the PCB top face, Ø9.0 boss protruding 2.6 mm into a Ø9.3 NPTH; land pattern Ø13.0 annular pad; KiCad libraries published Not verified this pass
  • Reverse geometry: the flange solders to the top of the PCB and the stud enters from the back of the board, through the Ø9.3 hole, into the boss. On a 2.0 mm board the boss's entry face sits 0.6 mm proud of the back face (2.6 mm protrusion vs 2.0 mm board).
  • The thread is a through thread (drawing check 2026-10-26, sectional A-A): M6 along the full 5.6 mm part height — it cannot bottom out, which inverts the press-fit engagement problem (see the thread-engagement section): the receptacle can seat face-to-face on the boss entry face, and any stud excess simply protrudes above the flange on the component side (up to 5.1 mm if fully seated) — a keep-out to plan, not a seating failure.
  • Engagement: max 5.6 mm = 5.6 turns = 0.93×d — marginally under the 1.0×d rule of thumb the press-fit M6 meets exactly (6.0 mm), in exchange for a seatable, soldered joint with a published torque.
  • Caveats: Würth's general line (not the automotive-released 786 series); the drawing prints only “M6” with no pitch (coarse ×1.0 by convention, which would match Amphenol's M6×1.0 — unverified); 85 A is a 20 °C rating, so the 60 A at under-hood ambient case still needs the usual thermal validation. M6 only — there is no M8 WP-SMRT.
  • Sibling correction: 746600165 (“Reverse with internal through-hole”) is not a threaded variant — its bore is a plain Ø6.5 mm clearance hole (drawing check 2026-10-26). Not a boss; noted so the similar number isn't mistaken for one.

Würth markets press-fit as the more reliable process at this current (gas-tight joint, no thermal stress; their literature claims FIT up to 30× better than SMD). Right-angle bosses — thread axis parallel to the PCB (checked 2026-10-25)

If the PCB sits perpendicular to the input panel — the orientation the right-angle output headers already imply — the SurLok stud axis runs parallel to the board, and the boss thread must be horizontal. Würth's REDCUBE press-fit line has that form:

  • WP-RAFU (right-angled, full-plain pin-plate U-block) and WP-RATR (right-angled, two-row pin plate): internal thread M3–M10 per Würth's family flyer — covers M6 and M8. Datasheet values across the RA family: rated current 160–350 A (74611134: 250 A; 74611164/174: 350 A; 7461063 RATR: 160 A at M4), PCB thickness 1.6–3.2 mm on every RA datasheet checked, brass/tin, −55…+150 °C.
  • M8 verified at order-code level: 7461068 (full-plain RA, 250 A) per distributor listing (Mouser ↗); a two-row M8 (7461108, 240 A) exists but is discontinued. M6 pinned (datasheet check 2026-10-26): WP-RAFU 7461114 (full-plain, 250 A, 3.9 N·m) and WP-RATR 7461106 (two-row, 240 A, 3.9 N·m) — distributor stock/pricing not yet checked.
  • Torque: Würth's press-fit design-guide permitted torques (M6 3.9 N·m, M8 9.0 N·m) cover Amphenol's stud torques (3.0; 7–8 / 8.5 N·m) — the M8 1,500 V case (8.5 ± 0.1 N·m) runs close to the 9.0 limit.
  • Caveats: (1) the RA parts are Würth's general press-fit line (7461xxx) — RoHS/REACh only, not the automotive release + 100 % inspection of the vertical 786 series; (2) Würth's own handling note: right-angled press-fit versions must be fixed and held in position while the screw is tightened, or the PCB can be damaged — the stud torque needs a fixture or hold feature in assembly; (3) the thread centerline sits at a fixed, size-dependent height above the PCB surface (≈5.3–10.3 mm across the RAFU range; the M6 codes 7461114 / 7461106 sit at 8.0 ± 0.2 mm) — the enclosure must land the SurLok stud centerline on it.
  • Second source: TE Connectivity Power Elements also offer right-angle female thread (M3–M12, massive press-fit zone; application spec 114-161211) — part-level ratings not checked. Würth also lists an SMT right-angle line (WP-SMRA); thread sizes unchecked, and the SMT family caps at M5 vertically, so M6/M8 is not expected there.

Assessment — bosses

  • The soldered-catalog-boss concept mostly does not survive the thread correction. At the real M6/M8 stud threads there is no rated soldered boss from any Western catalog — the single exception is the WP-SMRT reverse-SMT bush at M6 (85 A, above); the M4 parts that publish 47–85 A fit a thread the SurLok stud doesn't have, and there is nothing rated at M8.
  • Press-fit REDCUBE is the rated boss route for both sizes (M6 and M8, 250 A class, automotive line, torque headroom verified at M8). Accepting it means a press operation in the process — Karl's call.
  • The only solder route left is custom-turned (Sandum-class, M6/M8 to drawing) — un-rated, validation-gated, and still facing the 3.0 / 7–8.5 N·m assembly-torque question against a solder joint.
  • Size fork sharpened by the same datasheet: 5.7 mm threaded is a 1,000 V (−40…+105 °C) part as published; 8.0 mm is the size where 1,500 V threaded (+125 °C) exists on paper.
  • Still open: stud length (not in the series datasheet — measure from the SLPRAT-class part drawing or hardware), and Amphenol confirmation if a 1,500 V threaded 5.7 mm is wanted.

Thickness is a second hard gate on the boss choice: above 2.7 mm even the automotive press-fit REDCUBEs are outside their published range (and the THR parts cap at 2.0 mm), so the node60 board's final thickness belongs in the boss decision alongside thread size.

Combined window with the chosen headers (drawing checks, 2026-10-25): the output header's own drawing (AT13-2P-BMXX, Rev A2) states no board thickness — the bound is its solder-post length, 3.1 ± 0.4 mm, so the board must stay under 2.7 mm at minimum post length for the pins to protrude at all. The T1S header (ATM13-2P-BM04, drawing ATM13-2P-BMXX Rev A2) is the same construction at 3.05 ± 0.4 mm posts — under 2.65 mm worst case, marginally the tightest header bound. Stacked with the boss ranges: a vertical automotive press-fit boss leaves a 1.6–2.7 mm board window; a right-angle boss leaves 1.6–2.65 mm (ATM13 worst case governs). A 2.0 mm board sits inside every range and leaves ≥0.65 mm worst-case pin protrusion on both headers.

Thread engagement — SurLok stud length vs REDCUBE thread depth (checked 2026-10-26)

Karl's question: is the REDCUBE thread deep enough for the SurLok stud, so the mating portions make solid contact? Drawing-level answer: the press-fit boss threads are blind, with a full-thread depth of 6.0 mm (M6) / 8.0 mm (M8) — and the SurLok studs are longer than that (10.70 / 12.2 mm REF). The risk is inverted: engagement depth is adequate, but the stud bottoms in the blind hole ~4–5 mm before the receptacle can seat against the boss face, so the joint gets no face clamp. (The WP-SMRT row at the bottom of the table is the exception — a through thread, added 2026-10-26.)

Sources: Amphenol customer drawings 10-730187 Rev F (SLPRATPSB) and 10-730189 Rev F (SLPRBTPSB), “SCREW TYPE” views; Würth datasheets 786202106 / 786202148 / 7461068, page-1 sectional drawings (Würth's page-3 note: for a blind-hole thread, the drawing's thread-length dimension “defines the minimum screw-in depth of a screw”).

CombinationSurLok stud (Amphenol dwg)REDCUBE thread (Würth dwg)Max engagementStud excess
5.7 mm → vertical M6, PFIFUA 786202106 M6×1.0, 10.70 REF blind, 6.0 6.0 mm = 6 turns = 1.0×d 4.7 mm
8.0 mm → vertical M8, PFIFUA 786202148 M8×1.0, 12.2 REF blind, 8.0 8.0 mm = 8 turns = 1.0×d 4.2 mm
8.0 mm → right-angle M8, RAFU 7461068 M8×1.0, 12.2 REF blind, 8.0 ±0.2 8.0 mm = 8 turns = 1.0×d 4.2 mm
5.7 mm → reverse-SMT M6, WP-SMRT 74660016 (added 2026-10-26) M6×1.0, 10.70 REF through, 5.6 (full part height) 5.6 mm = 5.6 turns = 0.93×d n/a — through thread: excess protrudes above the flange (5.1 mm if fully seated)
  • Engagement depth itself passes. Full use of the boss thread gives 1.0×diameter in both sizes — the usual brass-in-brass rule of thumb. Allowing ~1 pitch of incomplete thread at each end (stud tip chamfer/runout, boss entry — neither is dimensioned on the drawings), full-profile flank contact is ≈4–5 mm (M6) / ≈6–7 mm (M8), still ≈0.7–0.85×d, with the partial flanks carrying too.
  • ⚠️ Pitch is unverified on the M8 side and may not mate at all. Amphenol calls the 8.0 stud M8×1.0 (fine); the Würth drawings print only “M8”, which by ISO convention means coarse M8×1.25. If the REDCUBE M8 thread is coarse, the 8.0 mm stud does not screw in regardless of depth. Confirm with Würth or a sample thread gauge before layout. (M6 is consistent: Amphenol's M6×1.0 is the ISO coarse pitch.) The 12.2 mm stud figure is the 1,000 V SLPRBTPSB; the Gen 2.5 1,500 V receptacle's drawing (thread + stud) is a separate check still owed.
  • No face seating — the stack-up must absorb the excess. Maximum engagement happens with the boss entry face held (stud − depth) away from the plane where the stud leaves the receptacle's rear boss: ≈4.7 mm (5.7) / ≈4.2 mm (8.0), plus ~0.5 mm of tip clearance so tolerances never trade engagement for bottoming. The boss is designed for a short screw clamping a lug onto its top face; the SurLok stud turns it into a thread-only joint with a standoff — retention is the receptacle's panel-mount screws, and preload comes only from torquing the stud against the blind-hole bottom.
  • Amphenol's torques do not transfer. The 3.0 N·m (M6) / 7–8.5 N·m (M8) figures in the SurLok series datasheet are for a nut clamping a busbar on the stud. Against a blind-hole bottom they are not an assembly spec — set the assembly torque by validation (joint contact resistance and a 60 A thermal soak at max ambient), and note Würth's boss-side maxima (M6 3.9 / M8 9.0 N·m permissible) as the ceiling.
  • M6 vertical boss is now pinned: 786202106 — □10.0 footprint, block 10.5 mm high (13.5 incl. pins), 180 A, 16 press-fit pins on a 7.62 pattern. M8 vertical 786202148: block 13.5 high (16.5 incl. pins), □14.0. Both blind-thread, brass/tin, −55…+150 °C, automotive-released.
  • The WP-SMRT row breaks the pattern (added 2026-10-26): its M6 thread is a through thread, so nothing bottoms — the receptacle can be drawn down until its rear plane seats on the boss entry face (which stands 0.6 mm proud of the back face on a 2.0 mm board), giving the face clamp the blind press-fits cannot. The trades: engagement caps at 5.6 mm (0.93×d vs the PFIFUA's 1.0×d), the stud's excess (5.1 mm at full seat) stands above the flange on the component side as a live keep-out, its pitch is unprinted (coarse by convention), and it is a soldered general-line part, not automotive-released press-fit.

Assessment

Surveyor's assessment, for the decision.

  • SurLok Plus 5.7 mm meets every stated requirement except temperature, as costed: 120 A (2× the 60 A design point), IP67 mated, tool-free service disconnect, deep stock at both distributors, ≈$41/device @100 — but per Amphenol's brochure the costed 1,000 V DC parts are rated −40…+105 °C; only the 1,500 V DC variants reach +125 °C (corrected 2026-10-24, see Route 1). It is Karl's Radlok idea with the sealing fixed; whether the 1,500 V variants (unsurveyed) or a temperature exception close the gap is Karl's call.
  • ePower-Lite 5.7 mm is now the only front-runner that matches every requirement as published (−40…+125 °C, IP67 + IP69K) and undercuts SurLok Plus slightly (≈$38 vs ≈$41/device @100) with one 2-pole housing instead of two single-pole connectors.
  • Radlok matches it on price and availability and loses on the one requirement that matters outside a battery box: the mated interface is IP40 and its ratings sit on an 80 °C basis with no published derating curve.
  • Studs & lugs are the cheapest honest route (Bussmann blocks ≈$29/device) and the friendliest to installers, but every part is temperature-unrated or capped at +100 °C — adopting it means accepting validation-by-test for the 125 °C ambient instead of a datasheet.
  • MCP 9.5 is the dark horse: one housing for both poles, TE truck pedigree, possibly ≈$15–25/device, and its contact rating checks out (78 A per TE) — its published −30…+100 °C temperature range is the noted potential concern against the −40…+125 °C target.
  • China channels repeat the output-clone pattern: genuine parts by P/N (cheaper than the US only at MOQ-50 tiers, and only for Radlok pins), ESS clones at $4–15 carrying claims instead of certifications, and studs at a fraction of US prices — all gated on the same sample validation as the DT clones.
  • Internal termination: the clamp-joint flavors are now all surveyed — SurLok's rears are closed at threaded/crimp/busbar (no screw-clamp exists), the only true screw-inside/connector-outside part at input scale is Harting Han Q 1/0 (≈$115+/device, IP65, −40…+125 °C), and internal screw blocks (ABB DBL80, $20.99) cover the gland-entry architecture.
!

Decision

DIRECTION SET by Karl, 2026-10-25: SurLok Plus with the threaded rear termination — 5.7 mm or possibly 8.0 mm — the stud screwing directly into a PCB boss (not the busbar rear). The boss survey is the section above, as corrected by the same-day datasheet check: the studs are M6 (5.7 mm) / M8 (8.0 mm), at which sizes no rated soldered catalog boss exists — except the WP-SMRT reverse-SMT bush at M6 (85 A) — the rated boss route is Würth REDCUBE PRESS-FIT (automotive line) at both sizes, the WP-SMRT is a rated soldered alternative at M6 only, and the remaining solder route is custom-turned (validation-gated). Still open within the direction: 5.7 vs 8.0 mm; the voltage class — noting that threaded 5.7 mm is a 1,000 V (−40…+105 °C) part as published while 1,500 V threaded (+125 °C) exists on paper at 8.0 mm; and press-fit vs custom-solder for the boss.

Survey history: completed 2026-10-23 undecided; the TE MCP 9.5 spec check was run (Route 5: current verified 78 A, temperature recorded as a potential concern at Karl's direction, route retained); ePower-Lite (Route 6) was the only all-requirements front-runner until Karl set the SurLok-threaded direction on 2026-10-25.
